text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 - prefix-cache hit-rate dropped from ~92% to ~18% across us-east-1 at ~11:02 UTC. Multiple customer requests experiencing 3-5x latency and occasional 503s. Paging oncall.

alex: saw the alert. I'm on it, grabbing traces & KV metrics.

priya: I'm collating recent deploys — nothing merged to runtime in the last 6h. Only config change was an autoscaler policy tweak at 09:50 UTC (no cache flags).

jordan: taking lead on infra. Oncall handoff in 15m if needed. Priorities: (1) confirm blast radius, (2) mitigate customer impact, (3) gather logs for RCA.

maria: CS reports from Charlotte and a few EU customers with higher latency; some call this "stuck generation". No data loss reported but UX timeouts hit.

alex: quick checks: prefix cache miss rate across all clusters: `hit_rate_by_prefix` shows a sharp drop for short prefixes (len 4-8). Full metric snapshot:
```
prefix: "the " -> hit_rate 0.14
prefix: "Hello" -> hit_rate 0.11
prefix: "User:" -> hit_rate 0.19
overall prefix hit_rate: 0.18 at 11:03 UTC
```

sam: I'm pulling KV cache server logs (kv-cache-proxy). I see a burst of `cache_invalidate` events around 11:01 UTC for keys with pattern `prefix:*`. Sample: 
```
[2025-10-21T11:01:03Z] INFO cache_invalidate key=prefix:abcd reason=eviction source=LRU
[2025-10-21T11:01:03Z] INFO cache_invalidate key=prefix:Hello reason=manual_flush source=orchestrator
```

priya: who invoked manual_flush? We didn't run any manual invalidate in Console. Could be an automated job. Checking scheduler logs.

jordan: mitigation options: (A) temporary increase cache size on affected pools, (B) roll back any recent orchestrator config that can trigger flushes, (C) fall back traffic to secondary region with healthy cache. Immediate: try (A) and (C) in parallel.

alex: increasing cache pool memcap for us-east-1 prefix shard 3 -> 6GB (command pasted to ops channel). Will monitor hit-rate.

incident-bot: action log: alex executed `cachectl set-memcap --pool=prefix-shard-3 --size=6G` at 11:07 UTC.

maria: CS: pushing proactive message to impacted customers: "We're investigating increased latency for generation requests; temporary mitigation underway."

sam: scheduler logs show a cron job `daily-index-rotate` had a bug: it uses a glob that accidentally matched `prefix:*` keys and issued `SCANS` with `--flush-matching` at 11:01. Looks like the job was retriggered due to a missed run earlier.

priya: that explains the `manual_flush` source=orchestrator entries. We need to patch the cron to exclude `prefix:` keys and add a safety gate.

jordan: metrics update: after memcap increase and aborting cron job at 11:09, prefix hit-rate climbed to ~56% by 11:12, and latency dropped ~2x. Still not back to baseline.

alex: added a short-term workaround: enable greedy KV reuse on runtime so stale KV entries are reused if re-warm fails. Command: `runtimectl set-param --kv-reuse=aggressive` executed 11:10. This reduces miss amplification while caches refill.

maria: are there any customers with errors (503)? Need list for SRE to follow up.

sam: pulled request logs: ~0.6% 5xx spike between 11:02-11:09, primarily upstream 503s when cache lookups timed out. Attached sample log lines: 
```
2025-10-21T11:04:12Z GET /v1/generate  upstream_timeout cache_lookup key=prefix:Hello err=timeout
2025-10-21T11:05:01Z POST /v1/chat   200   latency=920ms note=cache_miss
```

priya: hypothesis tracking (in-thread):
- hypothesis 1: `daily-index-rotate` cron used a glob that accidentally invalidated prefix keys -> mass cache churn (supported by `manual_flush` logs).
- hypothesis 2: autoscaler policy tweak contributed by shrinking cache pool memory earlier -> amplified misses (no recent shrinkes observed).
- hypothesis 3: a separate leak / eviction storm caused by hot keys pushing others out (not primary given invalidate logs).

alex: current verdict: hypothesis 1 is primary root cause; hypothesis 3 secondary. We'll mark hypothesis 2 as unlikely.

jordan: next steps for RCA: 1) collect full scan of `cache_invalidate` events (already initiated by sam) 2) gather scheduler run history and who/what retriggered the cron 3) timeline of client-visible errors & SLO impact 4) reproduce small-scale locally if possible.

incident-bot: SLO impact estimate: 11:02-11:12 UTC 0.6% error increase and 3x tail latency for affected routes. Severity remains P1 until customers cleared.

maria: handing to jordan for next oncall. Jordan, I'll add a checklist for customer followup and retrospective notes.

jordan: I'm taking over the incident at 11:20 UTC. Oncall handoff: alex -> jordan. Please include any ephemeral commands in ops-runbook.

sam: uploading intermediary logs to secure storage: s3://redwood-incidents/1752001234/prefix-logs.tar.gz (internal link).

priya: patch created to add exclusion filter in `daily-index-rotate` and a safety flag `--require-confirmation` for destructive flushes. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/ops/+/1234 (will merge after post-incident review).

alex: full mitigation summary: aborted cron (11:09), increased memcap (11:07), enabled kv-reuse (11:10). Hit-rate 92% -> 18% -> 56% -> 89% by 11:30. Latencies largely normalized by 11:28.

maria: updating customers: sending follow-up that root cause was an accidental flush from ops cron and that permanent safeguards are being added.

jordan: leaving this thread for RCA writeup. Please paste collected evidence (logs, metrics graphs, PR link) in the RCA doc. I'll draft timeline and corrective actions.

alex: pasted quick timeline snippet for RCA doc: 
```
11:01 UTC - `daily-index-rotate` retriggered and issued flush-matching on `prefix:*` keys
11:02 UTC - Alerts: prefix cache hit-rate drop, latency spike
11:07 UTC - increased memcap on affected pools
11:09 UTC - aborted cron job
11:10 UTC - enabled aggressive KV reuse on runtime
11:28 UTC - metrics back to baseline
```

priya: adding postmortem action items: 
- add exclude-filter & safety flag to cron (owner: priya, ETA: 3 days)
- add canary run for destructive ops with manual approval (owner: ops, ETA: 1 week)
- enhance cache observability to emit per-prefix eviction reasons (owner: runtime team, ETA: 2 weeks)

maria: thanks team! I'll schedule customer debriefs and CS follow-ups. Closing P1 once RCA doc ready. :white_check_mark:
